case.amplicon_range_bp: 485 bp (revertant / excised allele) vs 717 bp (transformant / mimp1-containing allele); only the 485 bp product lies in a public accession
case.caveats: 1) The 485 bp figure is the REVERTANT (post-excision) product. The 717 bp transformant allele carries the mimp1 copy in niaD intron 1 inside engineered plasmid pNm1H18/pAN301 and is NOT represented in any public accession - do not expect 717 bp from M58291.1. 2) The reporter is an A. nidulans niaD gene deployed heterologously; the transposition experiment itself was run in Fusarium oxysporum, so the experimental host organism differs from the amplicon's template organism. 3) The paper reports 485 bp for a revertant, and excision footprints can in principle differ from wild type by a few bp; the exact, zero-mismatch 485 bp match against wild-type niaD is what makes this case externally verifiable. 4) No degenerate bases; neither primer spans a junction; single-locus, non-nested assay.

Transposition of a fungal miniature inverted-repeat transposable element through the action of a Tc1-like transposase. Genetics. 2007;175(1):441-452. doi:10.1534/genetics.106.064360. PMID 17179071; PMCID PMC1775018.
